Pages | File | Purpose | | --- | --- | | `index.html` | Portal home: three large icon-action buttons (Apply / Track / Pay); service-announcement list | | `apply.html` | Three-column layout: left step tree (6 groups + sub-steps, sub-steps show completed ✓ / current highlight / conditionally locked, completed steps are click-back-able); center current-step form (dynamically rendered: address, project type, scope, dates, parcel lookup, ownership, contractor, various file uploads, neighbor signature block, various affidavits, final review and submit); right sticky "What materials you'll need" dynamic checklist (updates ✓ as you progress / select) + estimated fee breakdown card (with expedited toggle); conditional visibility (exterior changes → neighbor step; historic parcel → historic-district step; Addition/Structural → elevation drawings; Roof/Electrical/HVAC → energy worksheet) | | `my-applications.html` | List of 3 past applications (status badges) |

run_plan.goal: Exhaustively explore and critique the UX of the CivicPort municipal permit portal, focusing on the complex multi-step application flow, conditional logic, adjacent tracking/payment pages, and responsive layout issues.
run_plan.summary: The run will start by assessing the homepage and adjacent pages (Fees, My Applications) to establish context and check for basic layout issues. The core of the exploration will dive deeply into the 6-step apply.html form, specifically targeting conditional logic triggers (exterior, historic, structural, roof) to validate dynamic UI updates. Finally, the entire critical path and conditional states will be re-validated on a mobile viewport to assess responsive behavior and tap-target warnings.
assumptions: The apply.html form simulates dynamic state changes based on project type and parcel selection, as described in the prescan summary.
The 'Cancel' button on apply.html triggers the visible dialog and can be dismissed.
The 'Expedited review' toggle on apply.html updates the estimated fee breakdown dynamically.
Navigation links in the header are consistent across all pages despite current small tap target warnings.
risk_hotspots: apply.html: Conditional visibility logic (exterior -> neighbor step, historic -> historic step, Addition/Structural -> elevation, Roof/Electrical/HVAC -> energy worksheet)
apply.html: Unlabeled inputs on step 1.1 (Street address, Zip) causing accessibility issues
apply.html: Dynamic updates to the 'What you'll need' checklist and 'Estimated fees' card
Global: Small tap targets on header navigation links (Apply, My applications, Fees, Help) failing mobile guidance
